Definition: (only in plural as abstract) adolescence; figuratively, vigor
BiblicalUsage: Youth, adolescence, and figuratively vigour, and the Bible uses it for the strength that returns. The restored city is told she shall forget the shame of her youth, and shall not remember the reproach of her widowhood any more. And Elihu promises the sick man that his flesh shall be fresher than a child's, and he shall return to the days of his youth.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for youth carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the return in it, that shame can be forgotten and flesh can be made fresh again.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
